# @jpisgeek/imagegen

Generate local PNG graphics with FLUX.1-schnell through mflux and MLX on Apple
Silicon. The default is 4-bit weights, four inference steps and 1024 × 1024. No
frontier model, hosted inference service, or LM Studio is required.

**Version** `2026.11.18.1` · **License** MIT · **Source**
https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/tree/main/imagegen

## Install

Install the published behavior into your Swamp repository:

```sh
swamp extension pull @jpisgeek/imagegen
```

See [Mac setup](MAC_SETUP.md) before running the behavior. The package includes
an editable [workflow template](examples/imagegen.workflow.yaml). This installs
the adapter only, not mflux or model weights.

For source development instead, clone this repository and register the model:

```sh
swamp extension source add /example/slog-bog/imagegen --only models
```

| ---------------- | ------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `prompt`         | string  | yes      |         |                                                                                |
| `seed`           | integer | no       | `42`    |                                                                                |

| `imagePath`      | string  | no       |         | Optional local reference PNG/JPEG; ordinary img2img, not identity preservation |
| `imageStrength`  | number  | no       | `0.4`   |                                                                                |

## Example

```yaml
type: "@jpisgeek/imagegen"
name: imagegen
globalArguments:
  executable: /example/runtime/bin/mflux-generate
  modelPath: /example/models/schnell-q4
  outputRoot: /example/output
  timeoutSeconds: 600
```

## Caveats

This is a reconstruction of a previously used local image-generation approach,
not a recovered byte-for-byte copy. The historical dependency version and exact
implementation were not available. No private prompts, artwork or provenance are
included.

The adapter targets the mflux 0.24.0 CLI. It passes a local checkpoint with
`--base-model schnell --quantize 4`. Prepare all model and tokenizer assets
before offline use. It sets Hugging Face offline and telemetry opt-out flags;
missing assets must fail rather than download. These flags are not a network
sandbox. Test with networking disconnected for an actual offline acceptance run.

Optional `imagePath` uses ordinary image-to-image conditioning. It does not
guarantee character identity or exact reference style. There is no negative
prompt or guidance control because these are not useful schnell controls.

Swamp merges known global fields into method arguments during dispatch. These
fields are accepted for compatibility; execution uses the global configuration
in the method context, not per-method path overrides.

Each invocation creates a unique private output folder, a PNG, and a JSON
provenance receipt. Success checks the exit code, file type, bounded file size,
PNG signature and declared dimensions, then records a SHA-256. This is not a
full PNG decode or a visual-quality check. Review the image before use. Outputs
are not deleted by Swamp receipt garbage collection. Failed runs can leave
partial files; inspect and remove those manually.

Verification on Apple M5 with 32 GB memory: real Swamp text-to-image and
image-to-image runs passed with decoded, visually inspected PNGs and receipts. A
direct adapter invocation also generated a 1024 × 1024 PNG. A separate inference
process loaded a re-saved checkpoint and rendered successfully with network
access denied; a socket control confirmed the restriction. This does not
establish whole-workflow isolation or a machine-wide air gap, and the behavior
does not enforce network denial itself. See MAC_SETUP.md for exact versions,
checkpoint and scope. Unit tests also run on Linux.

## Security

The configured executable, Python dependencies and checkpoint are trusted local
inputs, not a sandbox. The process inherits the operator's permissions and
environment; do not configure an untrusted executable. No shell is used, and
arguments are validated. Paths must be absolute with no symlink components. Use
canonical paths: on macOS `/tmp` and `/var` are symlink aliases, and some
launcher paths are symlinks. Resolve them before configuring the adapter. Keep
output/model directories private and do not mutate them during a run. Offline
flags do not prevent a malicious executable from using the network.

Prompts, seeds, hashes and output paths are stored as Swamp runtime data and in
provenance.json, not logged. Use a local Swamp repository/datastore for offline
execution. A shared or remote datastore can transmit receipts outside the Mac
under that repository configuration. The prompt also appears in the process
argument list, visible to local process inspection. Do not use secrets in
prompts. Raw subprocess output is suppressed. Keep generated media, model
instances, receipts, local paths and model weights out of public commits.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for the registry release security review requirements.
